mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past 3 months compresses discount rates for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines for 3 consecutive months, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 0.5% for two consecutive months, it signals a tightening monetary policy that increases equity discount rates, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 0.5% for 2 consecutive months, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in unemployment rate and rise in nonfarm payrolls indicates a tightening labor market that boosts corporate earnings growth, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE falls and PAYEMS rises for 3 consecutive months, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In periods of strong GDP growth (GDPC1 above 2.0% annualized), the S&P 500 tends to produce positive forward returns as corporate earnings growth accelerates, particularly over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when GDPC1 growth exceeds 2.0% annualized, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in nonfarm payrolls over the past 3 months signals robust labor market conditions that support consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS increases for 3 consecutive months, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 90.0 for two consecutive months, it signals a weakening manufacturing sector that reduces corporate earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO < 90.0 for 2 consecutive months, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the federal funds rate and decline in unemployment rate signals a tightening monetary policy in a strong labor market, which increases equity discount rates without a corresponding earnings boost, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: monetary tightening in a tight labor market
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS rises and UNRATE falls for 3 consecutive months, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In periods of strong industrial production (INDPRO above 100.0), the S&P 500 tends to produce positive forward returns as manufacturing output supports corporate earnings, particularly over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO exceeds 100.0, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.
